title: Kettle Song (original) – live at the kitchen table
description: An original song, written the winter our heating broke. Just voice and guitar, recorded on a phone at the kitchen table. Lyrics in the transcript.

content.authorization_basis: Original synthetic transcript authored for the AI Video Discovery project. No real video exists.

segments.text: Hi. This is a song I wrote in January,
when the heating in our flat broke for nine days and
the only warm thing in the place was the kettle.
It's called Kettle Song.
It's just me and the guitar, recorded on my phone at the kitchen table,
so you might hear the fridge. Here it goes.
The radiator's quiet and the window's wearing frost.
I count the things I meant to fix and all the gloves I've lost.
But there's a little engine on the counter by the sink.
It rattles and it rumbles while I'm trying hard to think.
So put the kettle on, put the kettle on.
Nobody's coming but the morning, and the morning's nearly gone.
Put the kettle on, hold the cup with both your hands.
There's a kind of fire you can carry when the house won't understand.
My mother had a teapot with a chip along the spout.
She said you only pour the hurt in
once you've let the steam come out.
And I never knew she meant it till I stood here in my coat,
with a sentence for my sister that's still stuck inside my throat.

And the landlord says on Tuesday, and the landlord said that last week.
And the pipes have started knocking like they've got a word to speak.
So I'll call her after breakfast.
I will call her, yes I will.
I'll let the water settle and I'll let the room be still.

Somebody's coming with the morning, and the morning won't be long.

The heating's fixed now, by the way. I still haven't called her. Working on it.
